stem.text: The amount of water in a reservoir is modeled by the function \( W \), where \( W(t) \) is measured in millions of gallons and \( t \) is measured in months for \( 0 \le t \le 8 \). The function \( W \) satisfies the differential equation \[ \frac{dW}{dt} = \frac{1}{10}(W - 40)(t - 3). \] It is known that \( W(3) = 45 \) and that \( W(t) > 40 \) for \( 0 \le t \le 8 \).

parts.prompt: Find the value of \( t \), for \( 0 < t < 8 \), at which \( W \) has a critical point. Determine whether \( W \) has a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at this value of \( t \). Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: Set the rate equal to zero. The factor W - 40 is never zero because W(t) > 40.
So the only critical point is where the second factor vanishes.
For 0 < t < 3 the factor t - 3 is negative and W - 40 is positive, so dW/dt < 0. For 3 < t < 8 both factors are positive, so dW/dt > 0.
dW/dt changes from negative to positive at t = 3, so W has a relative minimum there.

points.criterion: Sets dW/dt = (1/10)(W - 40)(t - 3) equal to zero, uses W(t) > 40 to rule out the factor W - 40, and gives t = 3.

Concludes that W has a relative minimum at t = 3 because dW/dt changes from negative to positive there, with the sign on each side tied to W - 40 > 0 and the sign of t - 3. A conclusion from W''(3) > 0 together with W'(3) = 0 is also accepted. A bare conclusion with no sign argument does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Find \( \dfrac{d^{2}W}{dt^{2}} \) in terms of \( W \) and \( t \). Then find the value of \( \dfrac{d^{2}W}{dt^{2}} \) at \( t = 3 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate with the product rule; the derivative of W - 40 with respect to t is dW/dt.
Substitute the differential equation for dW/dt.

points.criterion: Differentiates the right side with respect to t, treating W as a function of t, so that the derivative of (W - 40) contributes dW/dt: (1/10)(dW/dt)(t - 3) + (1/10)(W - 40), or an equivalent form.

Writes d^2W/dt^2 in terms of W and t only, (W - 40)(t - 3)^2/100 + (W - 40)/10 or any equivalent form such as (W - 40)((t - 3)^2 + 10)/100. An expression still containing dW/dt does not earn the point.
Substitutes t = 3 and W = 45 into the expression and gives 1/2, or 0.5.

parts.prompt: Find the open interval, within \( 0 < t < 8 \), on which the graph of \( W \) is both increasing and concave up. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: dW/dt > 0 exactly when t - 3 > 0, because W - 40 > 0.
Both factors of the second derivative are positive for every t in the interval, so dW/dt is increasing everywhere.
W is increasing and concave up where both hold.

points.criterion: Gives the interval 3 < t < 8. Including one or both endpoints, as in 3 <= t <= 8, is also accepted.

Gives a reason covering both conditions: dW/dt > 0 on the interval because W - 40 > 0 and t - 3 > 0, and d^2W/dt^2 > 0 (so dW/dt is increasing) because W - 40 > 0 and (t - 3)^2 + 10 > 0. A reason that addresses only increasing or only concavity does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Find the absolute minimum value of \( W(t) \) for \( 0 \le t \le 8 \). Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: t = 3 is the only critical point in the interval, W is decreasing on 0 < t < 3 and increasing on 3 < t < 8.
So W(t) >= W(3) for every t in the interval, and the absolute minimum is at t = 3.

points.criterion: Justifies a global minimum at t = 3: W decreases on the whole of 0 < t < 3 and increases on the whole of 3 < t < 8, or t = 3 is the only critical point on the interval and it is a relative minimum. A relative-minimum argument with no statement about the whole interval does not earn the point.
Gives the absolute minimum value 45 (millions of gallons).
